title: Al-Mu'min, the Giver of Safety
hookLine: the Giver of Safety and faith

cards: Who would you call at three in the morning? Not the funniest friend or the smartest one. The safe one: the one who wouldn't tell anyone, wouldn't make you feel stupid, would just pick up.

Long before the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ received any revelation, the people of Mecca had a nickname for him. They left their valuables with him when they traveled. They called him al-Amin, the trustworthy one, the safe one.
Today's name comes from the same three letters, and you already know it as the word for a believer.

teach.b: The root is a-m-n, and it grows a whole family. Amn: safety, the absence of fear. Amanah: a trust, something left in your keeping.
Iman: faith. Amin: trustworthy. And the word Muslims say after the Fatiha, amin, so be it.
At the end of al-Hashr, after Peace, comes al-Mu'min. Pickthall translates it the Keeper of Faith, and scholars give the name two meanings that sit together.
First, the one who grants safety. The Qur'an says in Surah Quraysh that the Lord of the House fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear. Safety from fear is His gift.

teach.h: THE ONE WHO CONFIRMS AND KEEPS FAITH.
teach.b: Second, the one who confirms: who affirms the truth of His messengers and keeps faith with His promises. He never breaks trust. Now the surprise.
Mu'min is also the everyday word for a believer, a person of faith. The same word names Allah and names the people who trust Him. And the Prophet tied the two together in a very practical way.

Tirmidhi and Nasa'i record him saying: the mu'min is the one from whom people's lives and property are safe. Another hadith, in Bukhari: the Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand people are safe.
So a believer, in this sense, isn't first someone who holds the right ideas.

teach.h: A BELIEVER PEOPLE FEEL SAFE AROUND.
teach.b: It's someone people feel safe around.
The name tells you what the one you trust is like, and what the one who trusts is meant to become.

how: Muslims describe the believer, the mu'min, by how safe others are around them, and treat promises, secrets and anything left in their care as an amanah, a trust; al-Amin, the trustworthy, was the Prophet's nickname in Mecca.

o: the one who rewards every believer
the one who believes most deeply of all
the one who grants safety and keeps faith

games.q: the family of a-m-n — tap the pairs.
p: a trust left in your keeping

s: mu'min is used only as a name of Allah
it's also the everyday word for a believer.
the Meccans called Muhammad al-Amin before his prophethood
they left their valuables with him.
the hadith defines a believer by what they own
by whether people's lives and property are safe with them.

games.q: the Prophet describes the mu'min in one line. what does he say?
o: the one who prays the longest
the one from whom people's lives and property are safe
the one who knows the most
games.why: the mu'min is the one people are safe with, in their lives and property (Tirmidhi; Nasa'i).

practice: Remember a time you felt completely safe with someone, where you were and what they did or didn't do, and let the feeling come back into your body: the shoulders dropping, the breath getting longer. Stay there for a few breaths.

Then think of one person who might not feel safe right now, at home, at work, in their own head, and what would make them feel even a little safer around you: a kept secret, a calm voice, showing up when you said you would.

wordCard.voice: Al-Mu'min. The Giver of Safety, who grants safety from fear and keeps faith; also the word for a believer. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Giver of Safety, the Keeper of Faith; also, a believer. from a-m-n.

carryVoice: Your line: the one who makes safe. A kept secret is a small amanah. Rest well.

sources.ref: Qur'an 106:3–4 (who fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear)
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2627; Sunan an-Nasa'i 4995 (the mu'min is the one people's lives and property are safe from)
Sahih al-Bukhari 10 (the Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand people are safe)
Ibn Hisham, Sirah (al-Amin, the Meccans' name for Muhammad)
